findings.title: [cross-lane] ERP depends on five rs_console routes that neither contract doc lists (facebookPool.ts calls the console directly)
findings.evidence: The root Contracts row for /api/coordinator/* names only routes/coordinator.ts, vncBridge.ts and fleet/proxyHealth.ts, and trackers/facebook/AGENTS.md 'Forwarded today' lists PUT /v1/accounts/{id} as the credentials write only. But the pool's Assign flow (facebookPool.ts) calls callFacade directly for GET /v1/fleet, PUT /v1/accounts/{id} with fb_uid, secrets.fb_token and device_cookies, PUT /v1/workers/{id}/session, POST /v1/workers/{id}/restore-session, POST /relogin, and GET /v1/logins. Neither doc mentions /session, /restore-session, fb_uid, fb_token or device_cookies, and coordinator.ts's own ACCOUNT_FIELDS (coordinator.ts:261-264) leaves out fb_uid and fb_token. So a reader of the ERP side would conclude the ERP never sends them. rs_console has tests for these routes (tests/test_console.py), but the doc that tells a console maintainer what the ERP depends on is incomplete.
findings.failure_scenario: A console change that tightens ACCOUNT_WRITE_FIELDS to match coordinator.ts, or that renames or removes /v1/workers/{id}/session or /restore-session as unused by the ERP, passes the console's suite. After deploy, every pool Assign either drops fb_uid, so the worker signs in the new account from the previous account's device identity, or falls back from cookie-first to a password Re-login, which is a Facebook login from the worker IP and the checkpoint risk the root AGENTS.md calls the first rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Add facebookPool.ts (and the five routes, with fb_uid / fb_token / device_cookies on PUT /v1/accounts) to the AGENTS.md Contracts row and to trackers/facebook/AGENTS.md 'Forwarded today'. Name apps/backend/tests/facebook-pool.test.ts as that contract's test.
findings.regression_test: A doc-lint test that greps apps/backend/src for callFacade/fetch paths under /v1/ and asserts each one appears in trackers/facebook/AGENTS.md.

findings.title: Coordinator proxy keeps two allowlisted routes no UI calls, one of them a credential write
findings.evidence: No file in apps/frontend/src calls /api/coordinator/stats/reviews or /api/coordinator/accounts/ (grep). Only coordinator-cache.test.ts and coordinator-routes.test.ts reach them. The pool's Assign writes accounts through callFacade in facebookPool.ts instead. The header comment says the allowlist exists so the UI reaches only what it needs.
findings.failure_scenario: PUT /api/coordinator/accounts/:id stays a manager-reachable path that can overwrite any vault account's password, TOTP and email secrets with no UI, no pool-ledger event and no account_no audit row. Pool Assign writes the same data with an audit row. A stolen manager session, or a script, uses the unaudited door.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop both routes and their tests, or wire them to a page. If the credential form is planned, record it in a ticket.
findings.regression_test: The coordinator-routes allowlist test asserts 404 for PUT /api/coordinator/accounts/x and GET /api/coordinator/stats/reviews.

findings.title: Reddit proxy forwards rule create/edit/delete that no UI calls
findings.evidence: trackerApi exposes only listRules. DesktopTracker.tsx calls listRules at :100 and :181 and nothing else. POST /rules, PATCH /rules/:id and DELETE /rules/:id are still proxied. Every allowlist entry exists on the tracker (api.ts:250-289), so none is a dead 404. These three are unused write surface.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager session (or anything holding one) can add or enable rules that are appended to the live eval prompt (prompts.ts liveConfig) with no UI showing it. That silently changes the live prompt version and splits its scores, which the tracker's AGENTS.md says must go through a candidate trial.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the three write routes from tracker.ts (and the root/trackers/reddit AGENTS.md lists), or add the rule editor they were meant for.
findings.regression_test: tracker-routes.test.ts 'rejects paths outside the allowlist' asserts POST /api/tracker/rules is 404.

findings.title: Shared HeartbeatAnswer type omits the 'resume' directive and resume_id the backend sends
findings.evidence: fleet.ts declares directives: Array<'relogin'> and only relogin_id. claim.ts answers directives [...'relogin', ...'resume'] and resume_id. fleet.ts itself defines FLEET_RESUME_SINCE for 'the first worker build that takes the resume directive'. No TS code imports HeartbeatAnswer, so the compiler never catches the drift.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone writing a TS consumer of the heartbeat (a test fake, the host agent port, an ERP-side simulator) types it from the shared file and narrows on 'relogin'. A Mark healthy then reaches a parked worker as an unknown directive and is ignored, and the worker stays parked.
findings.proposed_fix: directives: Array<'relogin' | 'resume'>; add resume_id?: string; annotate claim.ts's answer as HeartbeatAnswer so tsc enforces it.
findings.regression_test: Type the heartbeat route's c.json payload with `satisfies HeartbeatAnswer`; typecheck fails on drift.

findings.title: ERP worker-id regex refuses '.' that the console and the VNC route accept
findings.evidence: coordinator.ts WORKER_ID is ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$, but VNC_WORKER_ID in the same file and the console's _WORKER_ID both allow '.'. WORKER_ID gates /workers/:id/logins, /cities, /queue and /city-log. Today's fleet.toml ids (ne-1, se-1, mw-1, sc-1, denver-1, wc-1) have no dot, so nothing breaks yet.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker named with a dot (e.g. after an IP-like or versioned id such as 'w-10.60.14') appears on the Fleet page and can be watched over VNC. But its History, Edit cities, queue toggle and city log all answer 400 'Not a valid worker id' from the ERP, though the console would accept them.
findings.proposed_fix: Use one exported worker-id regex (the console's) for every coordinator.ts route, ideally from packages/shared.
findings.regression_test: coordinator-routes test: GET /api/coordinator/workers/a.b/logins is forwarded, not 400.

findings.title: Proxy round's 30 s console timeout is shorter than the console's worst case when many proxies are down
findings.evidence: The console probes unique proxies 8 at a time (CHECK_CONCURRENCY) with an 8 s lookup timeout, after composing /v1/fleet. The ERP aborts at CONSOLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30 s and then records coordinator = 'unreachable' with no rows.
findings.failure_scenario: With 25 or more distinct proxy ports dead or timing out, the console needs at least 4 waves × 8 s = 32 s, so the ERP aborts. The Proxies tab then shows 'console unreachable' and drops every coordinator row, at exactly the moment the operator needs to see which proxies are down.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the ERP timeout exceed ceil(ports/8)*8 s plus the fleet composition (e.g. 60 s, within Cloudflare's 100 s), or have the console cap its total probe time and return partial rows marked timed out.
findings.regression_test: fleet-proxy-health.test.ts: a fake console that answers after 31 s still yields coordinator 'ok' rows.

carryover.evidence: vncBridge.ts:49-53 sets MAX_BUFFERED, MAX_FRAME_BYTES (wss maxPayload at :268) and MAX_PENDING_BYTES. The client→upstream bufferedAmount check is at :163, the pending-byte cap at :169-174, and the upstream→browser check at :213. No regression.
Owned by the auth lane. The VNC side re-admits through the app every 60 s (vncBridge.ts:241-257, :310), so it inherits whatever authMiddleware decides about revoked families. Not re-verified here.

notes: Contract tests: I ran tracker-routes, coordinator-routes, fleet-proxy-health and wechat-market, plus vnc-bridge, coordinator-cache and facebook-pool, against my own PG18 (review1031-A8, :55608) after baseline DONE. Result: 7 files, 136/136 passed in 26 s. The full baseline run (backend-test rc=1, 1218 s) marks wechat-market, vnc-bridge and fleet-proxy-health failed, but those are 'Hook timed out in 30000ms' under suite load (23 timeouts in the log), not contract failures; they pass in isolation. Allowlist check: every ERP route in tracker.ts maps to an existing route in trackers/reddit/src/api.ts, and every coordinator.ts, vncBridge (ticket and ws) and proxyHealth path maps to an existing rs_console route, so there are no missing or 404 entries. Unused entries: A8-02 and A8-03. Console routes the ERP deliberately does not forward: /v1/queue/shadow and the dashboard. /session and /restore-session are reached only through facebookPool.ts (A8-01). Payload shapes: the Reddit types (matches, stats, workers, subreddits snake_case, prompt-stats, analytics, seen, prompt-candidate, promote, llm_model) match the tracker field for field. proxyHealth reads exactly the keys proxy_exit.py emits (ok, latency_ms, ip, city, region, country, org, error, url, workers). The memtrade ErpDay/ErpPoint/ErpLine/PriceStats types match WechatDayPush/WechatPoint/WechatLine/WechatPrice, buckets included. memtrade's normalize() nulls empty strings and rounds qty, which matches the ERP's strict str/count validators. Its stored-count check matches the ERP's cumulative stored_points, and the (report_date, post_key, item_index) PK is the same on both sides. Shared enum vs SQL CHECK parity verified: CLOSE_REASON_IDS (0057), CARRIERS (0094), PACKAGE_SOURCES (0106), AFTER_SALES statuses and resolutions (0175). Limits: ramPartDecode.ts and ramSheetSegment.ts were read for structure and hot paths, not every decoder table. Not checked: deployed prod/console versions, whether memtrade on the office Mac runs the erp.ts I read (its git repo has no commits), the memtrade test suite, the rs_console suite. Contract tests are ERP-side with mocked upstreams, so no automated test pins the tracker's or console's real response shapes to the ERP types; that drift is caught only by hand reviews like this one.
